## Read in single-cell information from TMA-based RCC study
based on [SingleCellExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SingleCellExperiment.html)

### steinbock generated data
The `read_steinbock` function provided by `imcRtools` can now be used to read in
`steinbock` generated data. 

```{r read and inspect steinbock}
sce <- read_steinbock("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/",intensities_folder = "intensities",regionprops_folder = "regionprops", graphs_folder = "neighbors",return_as = "sce")
sce
```

## Single-cell processing

We can set the `colnames` of the object to generate unique identifiers per cell and also set `rownames` to a clean target name.

```{r set-col-rownames}
colnames(colData(sce))
colnames(sce) <- sce$cell_id <- paste0(sce$sample_id, "_", sce$ObjectNumber)
rownames(sce) <- rowData(sce)$clean_target
```

### Add metadata 

It is also often the case that sample-specific metadata are available externally. This metadata is available as an external excel file:

```{r add metadata, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Read in external metadata
patient_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/data/Metadata_combined_RCC.csv",col_names = TRUE)
patient_meta$TMA_id <- str_replace(paste0(patient_meta$grid,"x",patient_meta$x,"y",patient_meta$y),"NA","")
patient_meta$TMA_id <- str_replace(patient_meta$TMA_id, "x","X")
patient_meta$TMA_id <- str_replace(patient_meta$TMA_id, "y","Y")
patient_meta[is.na(patient_meta$x),]$TMA_id <- "CX7Y8" #was missing in data

# Read in images
images_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/images.csv",col_names = TRUE)
images_meta$names <- str_split(images_meta$image,".tiff",simplify = TRUE)[,1]
images_meta$TMA_id <- str_split(images_meta$acquisition_description," ",simplify = TRUE)[,1]

images_meta$PID <- patient_meta$PID[match(images_meta$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]

#Add metadata to sce

## 1. Add PID based on images
sce$PID <- images_meta$PID[match(sce$sample_id, images_meta$names)] 

## 2. Add all other metadata based on metadata file
meta_add <- colnames(patient_meta)[!colnames(patient_meta) %in% c("PID","grid","x","y","spot","no_tissue","sample_id")]

patient_meta <- as.data.frame(patient_meta)
              
for (entry in meta_add) {
  colData(sce)[,entry] <- patient_meta[,entry][match(colData(sce)[,"PID"],patient_meta[,"PID"])]
}
```

```{r}
# Check whether every sample (and cell) is associated with a PID
unique(sce[,is.na(sce$PID)]$sample_id)
unique(sce[,is.na(sce$sample_id)]$sample_id)
```


### Transform counts

Problem: Right-skewed distribution (bias from highly expressing cells)
Solution: Count transformation using an inverse hyperbolic sine function (arcsinh; common in flow cytometry) = leads to linear-like scale near zero and log-like scale beyond a threshold (`cofactor`)
We apply a `cofactor` of `1`. 

```{r transform-counts, message=FALSE}
#Select 5 samples
id <- colData(sce) %>% as.data.frame %>% select(sample_id) %>% unique %>% slice(1:5) %>% pull(sample_id)

#Raw counts
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD45RO_RA", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "counts")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD68", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "counts")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD163", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "counts")


#Transformed counts
assay(sce, "exprs") <- asinh(counts(sce)/1)

dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD45RO_RA", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "exprs")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD68", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "exprs")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD163", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "exprs")
```

### Define interesting channels

Subset markers of interest for downstream analysis.

```{r select-features}
rowData(sce)$use_channel <- !grepl("DNA|H3|clCAS_PARP", rowData(sce)$clean_target)
```


### Define color schemes

We will already at this point define color schemes for different metadata
entries which will be helpful for downstream data visualizations. 

```{r color-scheme}
colors <- readRDS("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/color.rds")
colors

metadata(sce)$colors <- colors
```

## Save single cell object for downstream analysis

```{r save-objects-read-data}
saveRDS(sce, "/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/sce_MY_01.rds")
```

## Re-save images and masks 

Note that images and masks were loaded, modified and saved in the [MY_00_seg_QC.Rmd]() script. 

```{r}
images <- readRDS("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/images.rds")
masks <- readRDS("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/masks.rds")

all.equal(names(images), names(masks))
all.equal(names(images), mcols(images)$sample_id)
all.equal(names(masks), mcols(masks)$sample_id)
```

```{r}
saveRDS(images, "/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/images.rds")
saveRDS(masks, "/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/masks.rds")
```
